title: How to Build a Retirement Income Plan for a Long Retirement (30+ years)
description: Planning for longevity: Inflation, healthcare, and portfolio survival.
content:
Retiring at 60 and living to 95 means your money has to last 35 years. That is longer than many people worked. A 'Long Retirement' faces two main enemies: **Inflation** (prices doubling every 20 years) and **Sequence Risk** (a crash early on). You cannot just buy bonds and hope for the best. You need a portfolio that grows aggressively enough to beat inflation, but is safe enough to survive a decade of stagnation. This guide explains the 'Endurance Portfolio'.

Key Takeaways

  • Lower Withdrawal Rate: The 4% Rule assumes 30 years. For 35-40 years, the safe withdrawal rate drops to 3.3% - 3.5%. You need a larger nest egg.
  • High Equity Exposure: You cannot reduce stocks to 20% at age 65. You need 50-60% stocks to ensure your portfolio has the horsepower to fund your 90s.
  • Deferred Income: Buying a longevity annuity (QLAC) that starts paying at age 85 acts as insurance against living too long. It guarantees you won't be destitute in extreme old age.
  • Flexibility is Key: The ability to spend less in bad years is the single biggest factor in success. Rigid spending plans fail over long horizons.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Social Security is inflation-adjusted. Maximizing this benefit (by delaying to 70) is the foundation of a long retirement. It provides an increasing floor of income that never runs out.

The 35-Year Simulation

Why standard advice fails for long lives.

The Inflation Problem

At 3% inflation, $50,000 of purchasing power requires:

  • Year 1: $50,000.
  • Year 20: $90,000.
  • Year 35: $140,000.

Your withdrawal amount must triple in nominal terms. Bonds paying 4% fixed interest cannot support this. Only stocks can.

The 'Rising Equity' Glidepath

Instead of getting safer as you age, research suggests you should get riskier.
Start of Retirement: 50% Stocks (Safety first).
Age 85: 70% Stocks (Growth for late life/heirs).
This helps the portfolio keep up with the compounding cost of healthcare.

The Longevity Toolkit

  1. The 3-Year Cash Tent: Keep 3 years of spending in cash/short-term bonds. This allows you to ride out a Great Depression-style crash without selling stocks.
  2. Variable Spending Rule: "I will withdraw 4%, but if the market drops 20%, I will cut spending by 10%." This rule saves the portfolio.
  3. Invest in Health: The financial cost of frailty is huge. Staying mobile and healthy reduces the need for expensive custodial care. Health is an investment.
  4. QLAC: Use $200k of IRA money to buy a QLAC turning on at 85. It reduces RMDs now and provides a safety net for the 'danger zone' years.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is 4% ever safe for 40 years?

Only if you are lucky (Bull Market). If you retire into a 1970s Stagflation or 2000s Lost Decade, 4% fails. 3.5% is the 'sleep well' number.

What about nursing homes?

A long life increases the odds of needing care. You must have a plan: LTC Insurance, Home Equity release, or self-funding. Don't ignore it.

Should I leave an inheritance?

For a long retirement, prioritize your own survival. Tell heirs: "If there is money left, great. But my goal is to not run out." Spend your assets on your own care first.
